thread:
Maya Patel: heads-up — customer 'Northstar' opened a ticket: huge latency spikes and unexpected egress billing. they say traffic routed to us-west-2 even though account is pinned to eu-central-1. sample req id: r-0a1b2c3d
Devin Cruz: thanks, maya. do we have the router logs for that req id? also which fallback policy is enabled for their account?
Maya Patel: attaching minimal logs copy below from their support dump:
```
2026-02-28T14:10:12Z request_id=r-0a1b2c3d route=eu-central-1 -> queued
2026-02-28T14:10:15Z route_fail=capacity_exhausted shards=3 fallback=auto-reroute
2026-02-28T14:10:16Z routed_to=us-west-2 latency_ms=980 egress_cost=0.012
```
Devin Cruz: ok that matches our alarm — eu-central hit a hot-shard and the capacity manager triggered autospill to cheaper fallback pool which incorrectly allowed cross-region selection. ops-bot, did the recent routing table change include cross-region fallback weights?
ops-bot: routing-update v2026.02.25 applied to eu-central-1: fallback_pools=[eu-west-1, us-west-2], sticky_ttl=30s, allow_cross_region=true
Sanjay Iyer: ooof allow_cross_region=true is surprising for accounts with pinned_region. Was there an exception for Northstar?
Emily Chen: Northstar is on a 'soft-pin' policy (pin preference but allow fallback) — they didn't opt into strict-pin. But billing note: customers with soft-pin should get an alert before cross-region egress for cost-sensitive tiers. looks like that notification didn't fire.
Ivan Petrov: i'm seeing a short window where sticky_ttl expired and the routing decision fell back to global selector which has higher weight for us-west-2 under load. This created cross-region egress + extra token consumption due to retries.
Maya Patel: customer also reports a bunch of 5xx retries and double-charged embedding calls in their bill. they provided a sample timeline showing 3 immediate retries after 503s.
Devin Cruz: are retries client-side? our SDK does 2 retries by default on 5xx, yes. Combined with queueing there could be request amplification. we should confirm whether requests were queued (pending) before being retried, causing repeated queue positions.
Sanjay Iyer: repro plan: (1) simulate eu-central saturation with synthetic load, (2) set an account soft-pin, (3) observe router decision tree & sticky_ttl expiry, (4) measure egress routing and retry amplification. who can run step 1?
Emily Chen: I can spin up the synthetic runner. quick note: add header x-client-retry=0 to avoid client amplification when validating routing decisions.
Ivan Petrov: adding the routing config we should test with:
```
router.config {
  allow_cross_region = true
  sticky_ttl = 30s
  fallback_policy = "cost-weighted"
  max_queue_depth = 120
}
```
Devin Cruz: if we reproduce, mitigation options: (A) set allow_cross_region=false for soft-pin customers temporarily, (B) increase sticky_ttl to reduce mid-request churn, (C) add a pre-fallback alert that notifies billing/CS for potential egress impact.
Maya Patel: customer asked for immediate mitigation. can we apply A for Northstar? need ops approval.
Sanjay Iyer: approve A for Northstar as a targeted override. also put a temporary rule to suppress cross-region fallback for accounts flagged cost-sensitive.
ops-bot: change-request accepted. applying override for account northstar-acct-42: allow_cross_region=false -> in progress
ops-bot: override applied successfully at 2026-02-28T15:02:30Z
Ivan Petrov: follow-up: we should also patch the billing meter to dedupe rapid retry charges when they are client retries triggered by 5xx within a 5s window — filing a billing ticket.
Maya Patel: i've told customer we applied an override and to expect routing to stay in eu-central unless capacity prevents serving (then it'll queue). asked them to confirm whether latency improves. :crossed_fingers:
Devin Cruz: action items: Devin — run the saturation repro and post results; Emily — run synthetic load with x-client-retry header; Ivan — open billing dedupe ticket & check router code for sticky_ttl corner cases; Sanjay — coordinate targeted override rollbacks; Maya — own comms with customer.
Sanjay Iyer: estimated timeframe: repro & initial findings within 4 hours, billing ticket in 1 business day.
Maya Patel: customer replied: confirmed drop in cross-region calls immediately, seeing reduced egress line items. still monitoring latency for a bit. thanks team :heart:
ops-bot: incident-note created: INC-2026-0230 region-routing-cross-egress — assigned to Devin, Ivan, Emily
Devin Cruz: i'll post logs + graphs in this thread when done.
Maya Patel: closing loop soon, but leaving thread open until billing confirms dedupe and customer OK
Emily Chen: quick reminder — add the test case to our regression suite so routing overrides and sticky_ttl behaviour don't regress.
